summary.text: Earth's outer core is a fluid layer about 2,260 km thick, mostly iron and nickel, lying between the solid inner core and the mantle.
Its makeup is similar to the solid inner core's, but it stays liquid because the pressure there is not high enough to keep it solid.
Eddy currents in this nickel-iron fluid are seen as the main source of Earth's magnetic field, which protects life from interplanetary radiation.

facts.label: Depth range
facts.value: About 2,889 to 5,150 km below the surface

facts.label: Magnetic field inside
facts.value: About 2.5 millitesla, 50 times the surface field

facts.label: Freezing rate
facts.value: Inner core grows about 1 mm per year

facts.label: Time until frozen
facts.value: Roughly 91 billion years, by one estimate

items.prompt: What seismic evidence tells scientists that the outer core is fluid rather than solid?

options.label: Pressure waves cannot cross it at all
Earthquakes start inside it
Shear waves do not pass through it
All waves speed up sharply inside it

items.explain: Seismology shows shear waves are not transmitted through the outer core, which is evidence that it is fluid.

items.prompt: The inner and outer core have a similar makeup, yet only the outer one is liquid. What explains the difference?

options.label: There is less pressure in the outer core
The outer core contains far more water
The outer core is hotter than the inner core
Magnetism keeps the outer core stirred and melted

items.explain: The outer core stays liquid because there is not enough pressure there to hold it in a solid state.

items.prompt: As Earth's core slowly loses heat over time, what happens to the solid inner core?

options.label: It shrinks as it melts away
It stays exactly the same size
It breaks into separate pieces
It grows as liquid freezes onto it

items.explain: Cooling makes liquid at the inner core boundary freeze, so the inner core grows at the outer core's expense.

items.prompt: Measurements show the outer core is 5 to 10 percent less dense than pure iron would be at those conditions. What does this suggest?

options.label: The core is partly hollow inside
Lighter elements are mixed into the iron
The measurements must be badly wrong
The core is mostly made of rock

items.explain: Iron and iron-nickel alloy are too dense to match, so light elements are proposed as the feasible way to lower the density.

items.prompt: When liquid freezes onto the inner core, light elements are left out of the solid. What do they do in the liquid outer core?

options.label: Float upward while denser material sinks
Sink to the bottom and pile up
Escape straight out to the surface
Stay perfectly still where they formed

items.explain: The excluded light elements rise while denser elements sink; this chemical convection releases energy that helps power the magnetic field.

items.prompt: How does the strength of the magnetic field inside the outer core compare with the field at Earth's surface?

options.label: About the same strength
About 50 times weaker
About 50 times stronger
Zero, since the field forms in the crust

items.explain: The average field in the outer core is estimated at 2.5 millitesla, 50 times stronger than at the surface.
